Headline / Header: How Logs Flow from Collectors to Root-Cause Pinpointing
Visual Layout & Elements: Pipelined Flow Diagram: 7 Interconnected Stages with arrows, queue buffers, and latency tags.
On-Slide Content:
1. COLLECTORS: Fluent Bit, Vector, OpenTelemetry (OTLP), and Python SDK push logs to /v1/logs & /ingest-log.
2. ASYNC INGESTION: FastAPI validates API key and immediately writes to Valkey stream (XADD) in <2ms.
3. DRAIN3 MINING: Background worker streams logs through Drain3 tree miner, discovering templates and masking variables [<*>].
4. WINDOW EXTRACTION: 60s sliding window (30s stride) computes 12 features (entropy, error ratios, rate velocity).
5. ISOLATION FOREST: Pre-trained scikit-learn model evaluates window vector against optimal threshold (-0.075).
6. CAUSAL GRAPH: NetworkX engine traverses topological dependencies, computing blast radius and ranking root cause.
7. WEBSOCKET TELEMETRY: Broadcasts incident alerts, parsed logs, and topology updates to React dashboard (<120ms p99).
Key Metrics & Data Points: <120ms End-to-End Latency | 7 Processing Stages | Completely Non-Blocking
Design & Color Palette: Flow diagram with sequential numbered pill nodes, pipeline arrows, and glowing status tags.
Speaker Notes & Pitch Script: Here is how data flows through LogSentinel end-to-end: Logs arrive via OTLP or Fluent Bit into FastAPI. Instead of hitting the database immediately, they land in an in-memory Valkey stream. Our Drain3 worker parses them into templates on the fly. The feature extractor groups them into 60-second sliding windows. Our Isolation Forest scores the window; if anomalous, the NetworkX graph engine ranks which upstream service triggered the cascade. The entire sequence takes under 120 milliseconds.

Slide Title: Algorithmic Core: Drain3 & Sliding-Window Isolation Forest
Headline / Header: Unsupervised Intelligence Without Manual Regex Rules
Visual Layout & Elements: 3 Numbered System Component Boxes (01 Matrix/Miner, 02 Model Training, 03 Inference/Scoring) matching FlutterForecast Slide 13.
On-Slide Content:
[01] Online Template Mining (Drain3)
• Parses raw unstructured text into structured log templates in <0.5ms.
• Dynamically detects tokens, replaces variables with [<*>], and updates cluster prefix trees.
• Delivers 95%+ data compression while retaining semantic forensic fidelity.

[02] Sliding-Window Feature Extractor
• 60s windows with 30s stride extract 12 numerical & Shannon entropy features:
  - Statistical: log_count, error_count, warning_count, error_ratio, logs_per_sec
  - Entropy & Diversity: template_entropy, unique_templates, dominant_template_ratio
  - Topology: active_services, dominant_service_count, burst_indicator

[03] Unsupervised Isolation Forest & Threshold Sweep
• Ensemble of 100 isolation trees isolating anomalies based on path length.
• Optimal threshold sweep (-0.075): 0.940 Accuracy, 0.812 Precision, 0.867 Recall, 0.959 ROC-AUC.
Design & Color Palette: 3 Numbered component cards (01, 02, 03) with mathematical equation callouts and threshold curves.
Speaker Notes & Pitch Script: Our algorithmic core has 3 major components: Component 1 is Drain3, an online parse tree that strips dynamic variables and produces clean templates. Component 2 is our 12-feature sliding window extractor measuring Shannon entropy, error acceleration, and service distribution. Component 3 is our Isolation Forest. Through an exhaustive threshold sweep, we identified -0.075 as the optimal cutoff, achieving an outstanding 0.959 ROC-AUC and 83.9% F1-score with near-zero false alarms.
